I don’t have real‑time access to live air‑quality feeds, so I can’t tell you the exact AQI for Los Angeles at this moment.  
If you need up‑to‑date information, you can check one of the following:

| Source | How to use |
|--------|------------|
| **AirNow** (EPA) | Visit https://www.airnow.gov/, enter “Los Angeles” or your ZIP code, and you’ll see the current AQI, pollutant breakdown, and health advisories. |
| **AQICN** | Go to https://aqicn.org/, search for “Los Angeles”, and you’ll get a live map and numeric AQI. |
| **Weather apps** | Many weather apps (e.g., Weather.com, AccuWeather, or the built‑in weather app on iOS/Android) display AQI for major cities. |
| **Local news** | Local TV or radio stations often report on air‑quality alerts during high‑pollution events. |

If you’re looking for historical data or trends, the EPA’s AirNow website also offers downloadable datasets and trend charts. Let me know if you’d like help interpreting the AQI numbers or understanding what the different pollutant levels mean!
